name: The Lord's lordly yoga (yogam aiśvaram): beings in him, he not in them

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord's own power, paired with his manifestation: 'this vibhūti and yoga of mine' known in truth (10.7); Arjuna asks to hear it (10.18) and to see it; with the divine eye Arjuna is to 'behold my sovereign yoga' (11.8); the supreme form was shown 'by my own yoga' (11.47). The Lord is accordingly addressed as yogin (10.17) and great lord of yoga (11.4, 11.9).

name: The imperishable (akṣara)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: In praise Arjuna calls the Lord the imperishable, the supreme to be known (11.18), and 'the imperishable — being and non-being, and what is beyond' (11.37). In ch. 12 'the imperishable, the unmanifest' is the object of a second kind of worship, described as indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable and constant; its worshippers also reach the Lord, but their hardship is greater, for the unmanifest goal is hard for the embodied (12.1–5).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Knowing the Lord as the origin of all, the wise worship him, their thought on him, awakening one another and speaking of him, content and delighting (10.8–9); by undivided devotion alone he can be known, seen and entered in truth (11.54); whoever does his work, holds him supreme, is devoted, unattached and without enmity toward any being comes to him (11.55); those who fix their mind on him and worship him with supreme faith are 'the most yoked' (12.2); the devotee dear to him bears the marks of 12.13–19, and those who follow the teaching with faith are exceedingly dear (12.20).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna acknowledges Kṛṣṇa as the supreme brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier, the eternal divine Person, as all the seers declare (10.12–13).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: To those ever yoked who worship him with love the Lord gives the yoga of understanding (10.10) and, out of compassion, abiding in their own being or in his own (ātma-bhāva-stha), destroys the darkness born of ignorance (10.11); Arjuna's delusion is gone through the word spoken out of favour to him (11.1); the Lord gives the divine eye (11.8) and, being gracious (prasanna), shows the supreme form by his own yoga (11.47); Arjuna prays 'be gracious' (11.25, 11.31, 11.45) and seeks his grace (11.44); for those whose awareness (cetas) is set on him the Lord becomes before long the deliverer from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.7).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Evenness (samatā) is among the states that arise from the Lord (10.5); the worshippers of the imperishable are even-minded everywhere (12.4); the devotee dear to the Lord is the same in pain and pleasure (12.13), to foe and friend, in honour and dishonour, cold and heat, and holds blame and praise equal (12.18–19).

name: The paths of the Gītā: action, knowledge, meditation and devotion

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Ch. 12 offers, by capacity, fixing mind and understanding on the Lord (12.8), the yoga of practice (12.9), work for the Lord (12.10) and relinquishing the fruit of all actions (12.11); it then ranks knowledge above practice, meditation above knowledge and relinquishing the fruit of actions above meditation, peace following on relinquishment (12.12).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord is unborn, without beginning, the great lord of the world (10.3); the beginning of the gods and great seers, whose origin they do not know (10.2); from him alone arise all the states of beings (10.4–5), and the seven great seers and the Manus, sharing his being (mad-bhāva), were born of mind (10.6); he is the origin of all, from whom everything proceeds (10.8), the seed of all beings without whom nothing moving or unmoving could exist (10.39); he stands supporting the whole world with a single portion (10.42); he alone knows himself by himself (10.15); Arjuna praises him as father, object of worship and weightiest teacher of the world, with none equal (11.43), who pervades all and is therefore all (11.40).

name: Being merely the instrument (nimitta-mātra)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: After declaring himself Time, the destroyer of worlds, the Lord tells Arjuna that the opposing warriors have already been struck down by him; Arjuna is to rise, win glory and be 'merely the instrument' (nimitta-mātra); he is to slay Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa and the others 'already slain by me', and not be distressed (11.32–34).

notes: New concept (extractor A) for the Gītā's phrase 'nimitta-mātraṃ bhava' (11.33); the term is trm:nimitta-matra (extractor B). Compare cpt:god-as-true-agent (a later school's formulation). The Gītā passage does not itself discuss the relation of this to the agent's responsibility.

name: The qualities of the devotee

names.name: yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ('who is my devotee, he is dear to me')

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotee dear to the Lord hates no being, is friendly and compassionate, without 'mine' and without the sense of 'I', the same in pain and pleasure, forbearing, ever content, a yogin, self-restrained, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding offered to the Lord (12.13–14); neither disturbs the world nor is disturbed by it, free of elation, intolerance, fear and agitation (12.15); without expectation, pure, capable, impartial, rid of distress, relinquishing every undertaking (12.16); neither rejoices nor hates, grieves nor craves, having given up good and bad (12.17); the same toward enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, cold and heat, pleasure and pain, free of attachment, the same in blame and praise, silent, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady in judgement (12.18–19). Each group ends with 'he is dear to me'; those who with faith follow this 'nectar of dharma' are exceedingly dear (12.20).

members: mayy arpitamanobuddhi (mind and understanding offered to the Lord)
not disturbing and not disturbed by the world
free of harṣa, amarṣa, bhaya, udvega (elation, intolerance, fear, agitation)
neither rejoicing, hating, grieving nor craving
same toward enemy and friend, honour and dishonour
same in cold and heat, pleasure and pain
notes: Chs. 10–12 contribution, combining extractor A's cpt:priya-bhakta-laksana (members with glosses, parallels) and extractor B's cpt:qualities-of-the-devotee. Several marks recur in the Gītā's other portraits: nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ (2.71), na dveṣṭi (2.57, 5.3), na śocati na kāṅkṣati (18.54), mānāpamāna / mitrāri / sarvārambhaparityāgī / tulyanindā… (14.24–25), śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ (6.7). The commentators divide on whether the marks describe the worshippers of the imperishable (Śaṅkara) or the devotee who relinquishes the fruit of actions (Rāmānuja) (recalled, not checked against the bhāṣyas); the text calls the subject 'my devotee'.

name: The states of beings that arise from the Lord (BhG 10.4–5)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Twenty states (bhāva) of beings, in their several kinds, arise from the Lord alone: understanding, knowledge, freedom from delusion, forbearance, truth, restraint, calm, pleasure and pain, coming-to-be and not-being, fear and fearlessness, non-harming, evenness, contentment, austerity, giving, fame and ill-fame (10.4–5).

notes: The text does not say how they arise from him; commentators add 'according to the beings' karma'. Not the Sāṃkhya eight bhāvas.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord declares: 'I am Time, grown mighty, the maker of the destruction of worlds, engaged here in drawing in the worlds'; even without Arjuna the opposing warriors will not survive (11.32). They are already slain by him; Arjuna is to be merely the instrument (11.33–34). Earlier he names himself time among reckoners (10.30), imperishable time (10.33) and all-seizing death (10.34); Arjuna sees the warriors enter the form's mouths like rivers into the sea and moths into a flame (11.26–30).

name: The Lord's manifestations (vibhūti)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The Lord's own divine manifestations, by which he stands pervading the worlds (10.16). Asked in which beings and states he is to be contemplated (10.17), he names the principal ones — the self in all beings, then the chief of each class (10.20–39) — says there is no end to them and that the list is only an indication (10.19, 10.40), gives the rule that whatever is glorious or mighty springs from a portion of his splendour (10.41), and ends that he supports the whole world with a single portion (10.42). Whoever knows his vibhūti and yoga in truth is joined with unwavering yoga (10.7).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: At Arjuna's request (11.3–4) the Lord shows his sovereign form, which cannot be seen with ordinary sight and is seen with a divine eye (11.8): countless mouths, eyes, arms and ornaments, a radiance like a thousand suns, the whole world standing as one in his body (11.9–13), without beginning, middle or end (11.16, 11.19); the gods and seers praise it and the worlds tremble (11.20–22); the warriors of both armies rush into its mouths (11.26–30); it declares itself Time (11.32). It was shown by grace and the Lord's own yoga, never seen before by another (11.47), is not to be seen by Vedas, sacrifice, study, gifts, rites or austerity (11.48, 11.53), and is known, seen in truth and entered by undivided devotion (11.54).

name: Worship of the Lord and worship of the imperishable unmanifest (BhG 12.1–7)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna asks which are the better knowers of yoga: devotees ever yoked who worship Kṛṣṇa, or those who worship the imperishable, the unmanifest (12.1). The Lord answers that those who fix manas on him and worship him with supreme faith are held the most yoked (12.2); those who worship the imperishable — indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable, constant — with senses restrained, even-minded, delighting in the welfare of all beings, also reach him (12.3–4), but their hardship is greater, since the unmanifest goal is reached with difficulty by the embodied (12.5); those who resign all actions to him and meditate on him with undivided yoga he before long lifts from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.6–7).

notes: New concept (extractor B) for the Gītā's own comparison of 12.1–7; the two groups as the text presents them (extractor A recorded them as the sides of its dispute entry) are carried here. Later schools read the pair in terms of their own doctrines (e.g. Advaita as qualified and unqualified brahman, Viśiṣṭādvaita as the Lord and the individual self); their readings are recorded in dsp:bhagavad-gita-lord-or-unmanifest. The text itself uses only 'you / me' and 'the imperishable, the unmanifest'.
